title: How can a beginner create and animate pixel art NPCs for a game?
author: Billy_Tran112
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I’m working on a dark fantasy city-building game and want to create pixel art NPCs with their own personalities and appearances. Me and my brother are fan of LOTR and WH40K so i try to make a game for us to play.

I’m just beginner at drawing and pixel art. I’d like to start with a full-body NPC, then add subtle idle animations such as blinking, breathing, or slight hair and clothing movement.

What would be a good way to get started?

* Which beginner-friendly tools can you recommend for drawing and animating pixel characters?
* How should I choose the character’s size and level of detail?
* Is it practical to use AI as a starting point and then edit and animate the pixel art manually? If so, what tools would you suggest?
* How many frames would be enough for a simple idle animation?

I’d appreciate any advice or examples of workflows that have worked for you. Thanks!

comments.author: AbsentAgent
comments.body: Aesprite you can buy it on steam or your a.i can compile a copy for free.

comments.author: crackedpotstudio
comments.body: Generating assets and editing them to suite your own is currently something I’m also doing. I currently use Pixellab MCP in Claude and Aseprite to edit the files. I’ve posted a very early WIP on my account yesterday if you’re curious about how it looks.

comments.author: phantomimp
comments.body:
AI is very bad at doing Pixel Art. It gets worse the smaller your character becomes.

If you want to draw the art by yourself, pick 16x16 or 32x32 Pixels. 

If you want to generate them using AI, I'd recommend 64x64 or 128x128. Copy the AI Image into Aseprite and rezise it to the right format to get true pixel art. You will still need to manually remove artefacts.

comments.author: Borgware
comments.body:
I have been using pixellab for my project [https://hexwarren.com/](https://hexwarren.com/), while its descent for getting a base and directions, its harder to get good animation from it. To much of "prompt-praying" for my taste compared to how much "access" you get on their subscriptions. But it could be a good match if you are willing to use it as a starting point.

  
I have also been tinkering latley with claude to setup a sprite animation pipeline attaching a video on my progress. I start out with a description, the angle I was looking for and describe the details. Claude build a "system" for defining my character by creating a low polygon version that is then rendered into sprites. I am pretty happy with it so far, but then again I am no artist and wouldnt be able to paint something like this on my own.

https://reddit.com/link/1xmnocn/video/loiopcxlbdzh1/player

comments.author: CmdrCallandra
comments.body:
As long as you got at least 16gb vram gpu, I wrote a tool exactly for creating assets, being 3D or 2D. Essentially you would do a 3D model of you character, animate it, and then could make pixel art out of it, this way you always and up with the same base model / character. May like to take a look here

https://github.com/SifuInTheShell/Effigy

comments.author: snobesque
comments.body: Just use chat gpt to generate the spritesheets of pixel art animation. Choose the one you like and tune it. It is better then specialized services to start with and create first mockups
